title: Console & Tooling — Sprint check-in (scrapbook) 2026-03-11
content:
Meeting: Sprint check-in / ad-hoc sync (11:00 — 11:25)
Attendees: Aisha (notes/PM), Ben (frontend), Marta (rollouts), Ravi (observability), Lee (QA joined 11:10)

Purpose: quick pulse on UI polish, canary rollout status, and a short tie-in to analytics events for cost breakdown charts.

Quick wins / highlights
- UI: Ben shipped the header accessibility fixes (contrast + keyboard focus). Manual spot-check passed on Chrome/Firefox.
- Rollouts: Canary for v2 rollouts reached 35% traffic, no error spike. Automatic fallback not triggered.
- Analytics: First pass of token-cost breakdown events is in staging; we can see per-model token buckets but need to filter noise.

Deep dive items
1) Canary metrics and signal thresholds (Marta / Ravi)
- Observed: occasional 502s at ~03:12 UTC yesterday concentrated in eu-west region for model-x-quant.
- Hypothesis: multi-tenant scheduling edge case causing transient GPU OOMs. RH: infra ticket INF-2207.
- Decision: hold broad rollout until we have 48h without repeat; continue to ramp with circuit-breaker at 40%.
- Action: Marta to add an explicit rollback runbook snippet into rollout-playbook. Due: 2026-03-13.

2) UI rollout flags and feature gating (Ben)
- Problem: new routes toggle is embedded in build-time config which complicates rapid toggles for canary.
- Proposal: persist feature flags to the console DB and read at runtime for route toggles (lightweight cache + TTL).
- Concerns: small latency hit on first hit, but acceptable. Need DB migration plan.
- Action: Ben to prototype a cached runtime flag service and bench p99 latency. Due: 2026-03-18.

3) Analytics schema cleanup for cost charts (Ravi / Aisha)
- Current: events.token_cost has inconsistent model_name values (aliases). Aggregation breaks in dashboard.
- Ask: normalize model identifiers at ingestion (preferred) or add mapping layer in analytics pipeline.
- Action: Ravi to add mapping table and backfill last 7 days. Aisha to create accept criteria. Due: 2026-03-15.

Blockers / Risks
- QA backlog on canary test cases (Lee): need scripted tests for simultaneous ramp + region fallback. Blocker for 100% roll.
- Infra team capacity limited this week (on on-call rotations). Might slow down INF-2207 fix.

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Consider adding a canary heatmap in console: traffic %, p50/p95 latency, errors by region and model. Quick mock in figma.
- Short-lived tokens: if we enable runtime flags, we should add an audit trail for who flipped flags (security/compliance).
- Evaluate sampling for analytics events to reduce ingestion cost: keep full fidelity for rollouts window only.

Action items (compact)
- Marta: add rollback snippet to rollout-playbook (due 2026-03-13)
- Ben: prototype runtime flag cache + latency bench (due 2026-03-18)
- Ravi: mapping table + backfill for model ids (due 2026-03-15)
- Lee: draft canary QA playbook with test matrix (due 2026-03-16)
- Aisha: write accept criteria for cost chart normalization + link to dashboard mock (due 2026-03-15)

Follow-ups / next sync
- Quick follow-up check on Friday (2026-03-13) to see canary stability and mapping backfill progress.
- Add a short async doc outlining runtime flag design and DB migration options.

Misc
- Slack threads referenced: #console-rollouts (thread: 3 messages pinned), #infra-oncall (INF-2207 discussion)
- Links: rollout-playbook (confluence), ENG-4123 (feature flag RFC), PR #289 (console header fixes)

End of notes. Informal: felt lower friction today, keeping sprint momentum. Will push the flag prototype into a branch and tag folks for early review.
